title: Copper Review (2026)
intro: Google Workspace-native CRM for pipeline and relationship management inside Gmail and Google apps. This review covers verified 2026 pricing, core CRM capabilities, limitations, and who should buy — based on official first-party sources.
summary: Copper scores reflect first-party research — not hands-on product testing.
verdict: Copper is a strong choice when your sales motion lives in Google Workspace and you want CRM without leaving Gmail. Pricing is clear USD per seat; deeper enterprise customization is not the goal. Based on first-party research — not hands-on testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Google Workspace-native design keeps day-to-day selling inside Gmail/Calendar workflows many teams already know.
Pipeline and opportunity management are core Copper CRM capabilities.
Automation is solid for SMB Google-centric teams; less deep than full sales engagement platforms.
Native Gmail context is a primary strength for email-led selling.
Reporting covers SMB needs; heavier analytics buyers may outgrow Basic/Professional.
Configurable for Google-centric SMBs but not a Salesforce-class customization ceiling.
Deep Google Workspace native integration plus common sales stack connectors.
Workspace-native model reduces integration glue work versus bolting CRM onto Gmail.
Business tier helps mid-market; large enterprises often need broader platforms.
Clear USD ladder from Basic $23 annual; Professional is the practical tier for many teams.

bestFor: SMB teams standardized on Google Workspace
Buyers wanting native Google CRM vs Streak-lite tools
pros: Lower admin glue for Google shops
pricingSummary: No free plan. USD per seat/mo: Basic $29/$23 annual, Professional $69/$59, Business $134/$99. Free trial available.
limitations: Confirm live Copper checkout; packaging can change.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Copper when it matches your CRM buying criteria above.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Consider alternatives like streak, hubspot, pipedrive if fit is weak.
